method: Read-only inspection of the authenticated listing pages and product photos. Asking prices remain separate from third-party used-value evidence.

1624342312093126.condition: Seller describes it as used-like-new and barely used; photos show light surface dust/wear but no obvious impact damage.
1624342312093126.accessories: No USB cable, box, or power supply is shown or promised. It normally works over USB bus power; verify a USB-A-to-USB-B cable is included or budget for one.
1624342312093126.windows_status: Official Steinberg specifications include Windows 11 64-bit. Two D-PRE mic preamps, two combo inputs, direct monitoring, MIDI I/O, and 24-bit/192 kHz make it the best fit of these interface listings for simultaneous jam recording.
1624342312093126.research_notes: Exact model confirmed from the front-panel UR22mkII marking and rear USB 2.0/MIDI layout. At $30 it is below the current $38–$69 Reverb used estimate. Strong buy only after testing both inputs, headphone output, monitor outputs, MIDI, gain knobs, and USB connection.

1605979580884957.condition: Seller marks it fair and discloses damage to the main volume knob while claiming the unit still works. Photos show a heavily worn/dusty enclosure and visible control-area wear.
1605979580884957.accessories: No power adapter or FireWire cable is shown or promised. The rear photo shows FireWire ports and no USB port.
1605979580884957.windows_status: This is the original 24-bit/96 kHz FireWire-only UltraLite, not the later Mk3 Hybrid. MOTU's current Windows 11 installer support cited for the Mk3 Hybrid does not establish support for this original model. A modern Windows laptop would also need a compatible FireWire host/adapter chain.

market.source: Current eBay ask and archived Reverb listing context; not an exact sold range

1605979580884957.research_notes: The $50 price is explained by the original FireWire-only generation, fair condition, and damaged volume control. It is not a practical Windows 11 foundation for this setup; pass unless buying as a repair/legacy-computer experiment.

911094842057293.condition: Seller describes it as used-good but explicitly says the headphone jack is finicky/broken and direct headphone monitoring may be unreliable. Photos show cosmetic scratches on the red shell.
911094842057293.accessories: Original USB cable and box are included.
911094842057293.windows_status: Focusrite currently provides a Windows 10/11 driver for Scarlett Solo 2nd Gen. It has one microphone preamp plus one instrument/line input, so it cannot record two microphones at once.

market.source: Current used listing/market context for working units

911094842057293.research_notes: Photos identify the 2nd Gen layout (no Air control and older USB-B generation), not a 3rd Gen. A working unit around $50 would be reasonable, but $50 with a broken headphone jack is poor value. Pass unless it tests perfectly through monitor outputs and the price falls near $20–$25.

2021195761823060.condition: Seller describes it as used-like-new, excellent working order, and minimally worn. The listing includes a short demo video and multiple photos.
2021195761823060.accessories: USB cable/box inclusion is not clearly promised in the description; confirm before buying.
2021195761823060.windows_status: Native Instruments lists PC compatibility through ASIO/DirectSound/WASAPI. The official page names Windows 10 rather than Windows 11, so current Windows 11 operation should be confirmed with the seller or NI support. It provides two mic/line/instrument inputs and balanced monitor outputs.
2021195761823060.research_notes: The $70 firm ask plus $7.60 shipping is above the two recent Reverb sale examples. Good two-preamp design, but not compelling beside the local $30 UR22mkII. Offer about $55–$60 delivered, otherwise pass.
